[b]August 9, 2027: The Emperor and the World[/b]

Aïnthaar stands as an oddity among the nations of Erene and Northern Vespurias, its longstanding political institutions and strange economic and societal structures made it a lesser power by modern standards, guild feudalism still reigned as strong as ever, trade beyond the borders remained limited, and most GDP came from internal circulation of goods and services. Modernisation was slow with foreign goods being usually too expensive for the everyday individual. However, the tides of change had begun to occur as whispers of revolutions and seismic shifts in geopolitics began to filter into the markets and palaces of Aïnthaar.

Of course Aïnthaar had always been aware of the world around it, foreigners occasionally made appearances on the borders and in the ports, however, it tended to ignore world affairs, internal stability was far more important after all.

But as the 2020s began to enter their zenith, growing calls for more integration into world markets, world alliances, and the likes had caused stir among those of the Imperial high offices. It was now to this that the Emperor had been busy with since the beginning of 2027. 

The Emperor, however, today was not preoccupied with the matters of state, having taken a chance to vacation for the summer in the summer palace of the port city of Synhællen, a bustling metropolis of some 1.2 million citizens and the home of the major guilds of Aïnthaar.

The emperor sat within the inner courtyard of the ancient palace, a fountain throwing water out of the mouth of some fantastical creature lazily as the sound of the water quietly echoed through the courtyard. He had been reading some piece by one of the lords on taxation patterns in Aïnthaar, it was a long and dry piece of information describing nearly a millenniums worth of tax changes and economic systems, it wasnt that he enjoyed reading such things, but Aïn felt it gave his brain a chance to turn off and focus on something he really didnt care about, thereby alleviating the feeling of him having wasted time.

After a few more moments of reading the Emperor sat up from his seat, brushing the strands of blonde mane that had fallen into his face away with a hand he called for his advisor Tykón, shortly after being summoned there appeared a slender elven figure from behind a column, evidently having teleported there from some place.

Yes your holiness, stated Tykón with a bow towards Aïn.

I have a meeting today, with whatsit, Lord Harkonn, hm? he enquired.

Yes, I believe so, his lordship wanted to speak to you about education expansion, replied Tykón pulling a scroll from the folds of his billowing sleeves and unrolling it to read the contents therein. 

Yes, yes, I think we shall push that back, or at least send Erigath to handle it, replied Aïn with a wave of his hand.

Of course sir, replied Tykón with a nod, However, I do regret to inform your holiness that Mr. Erigath is out of state right now, 

You are right I forgot about that, so there is no alternative then? replied Aïn with a slight sigh.

Well, his lordship has been waiting months for this audience, your holiness, it would be most inappropriate to brush him off, replied Tykón.

Yes, but he is such a dreadful man, replied the emperor with a frown.

Of no doubt your holiness, and I shall see to it that the meeting goes quickly, replied Tykón.

Thank you friend, what time did he say hed be here? 

3:00, you have an hour, your holiness, 

Very good, I shall go on up then, if you will accompany me, replied Aïn rising from his seat.

Of course, stated Tykón, moving to follow him out of the courtyard.
